title: Open detail D4 · Black Belt's “Rubric and prices” tab has no prices
subtitle: A side finding from item 15d; for Black Belt's prompt. Item 15d's rule: a section's own settings stay in a tab named for what's in it. Black Belt's prices moved to each cycle (v0.902), so its “Rubric and prices” tab now holds the waiver, how long signed waivers are kept, and the default rubric — and its first line says “Prices are set on each cycle.” The Black Belt branch adds a fourth block there, the result emails (migration 0025, not merged yet), and keeps the name. Star's tab (picture 2) really holds its prices (“Fees”), next to its rubrics, grade scale, assistant-class table and result emails. (Preview screenshots · PC size, picture 5 a 320 px phone · fake data)

items.caption: 1. Black Belt testing → “Rubric and prices”: the first line says “Prices are set on each cycle.”; below it the waiver, the keeping rule and the default rubric.
2. For comparison — Star testing → “Rubrics and prices”: rubrics per Dan, grade scale, assistant-class table, Fees and result emails; the name says its two biggest things.

columns.label: Options B and C, drawn

items.caption: 3. Option B (recommended): “Rubric and waiver” — its two biggest things, rubric first like Star's; the result emails sit with them, as Star's do. The first line keeps “Prices are set on each cycle.”

row.caption: 4. Option C: “Rubric, waiver and emails” — everything it will hold once the result emails merge.
5. C on a 320 px phone: still fits beside “Cycles”.

columns.note: Pictures 3–5 change only the tab's words, drawn over the real page; nothing in the app was changed. The waiver's placeholder text (seeded by migration 0016) mentions “Rubric and prices”; it is replaced by the school's waiver before registration opens.

footer:
Your choice — one question: what should Black Belt's settings tab be called?
A · Keep “Rubric and prices”. + no work; the first line says where prices went. − the name points to prices that aren't there, against item 15d's rule; an admin looking for prices opens the wrong tab first.
B · Recommended: “Rubric and waiver” (picture 3). + names its two biggest things, like Star's tab; short. − the result emails (and the keeping rule) aren't in the name — as with Star's.
C · “Rubric, waiver and emails” (pictures 4–5). + names everything it will hold. − longer, and the name changes again if a block is added; Star's tab doesn't name its result emails either.
